subject: IB Diploma Computer Science
name: IB Computer Science
about: IB Diploma Computer Science teaching-hour plan. Hours from the IB guide; lesson durations share each topic's hours. Built by lessongen/ib_plan.py.
source: IB Computer science guide, first assessment 2027: recommended teaching hours (syllabus content SL 105 h, HL 195 h; case study SL 15 h, HL 30 h; internal assessment 35 h). Topic hours here share each group's hours in proportion to its understandings..

lessons.title: Inside the CPU: the ALU, the control unit, the registers and the three buses, and single-core, multi-core and co-processors
Primary memory (registers, cache, RAM and ROM), cache hits and misses, and the fetch–decode–execute cycle
The role of the GPU, and internal and external secondary storage (SSD, HDD, eMMC, optical, flash, memory cards and NAS)
Compression (lossy and lossless, run-length encoding and transform coding) and cloud services (SaaS, PaaS and IaaS)
CPU versus GPU: design philosophies, architecture, processing power, memory access and power efficiency, and how they work together
Pipelining: overlapping fetch, decode, execute and write-back, and how the cores of a multi-core processor work in parallel
Binary and hexadecimal integers, and converting between binary, hexadecimal and decimal
How binary stores integers, characters and strings, images, sound and video, and what that means for storage
Logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR) and their symbols, and combining gates into logic diagrams
Truth tables, Boolean expressions, Karnaugh maps and Boolean algebra to simplify circuits
The role of the operating system and its functions: memory, files, devices, scheduling, security, accounting, GUI, virtualization and networking
Scheduling algorithms (first-come first-served, round robin, priority, multilevel queue), and polling versus interrupts
Multitasking and resource allocation: context switching, resource contention and deadlock
Control systems: input, process, output and feedback; open and closed loops; controllers, sensors, actuators, transducers and control algorithms
Control systems in the real world: thermostats, lifts, washing machines, traffic signals, irrigation, security systems, automatic doors and autonomous vehicles
Interpreters, compilers, bytecode and just-in-time compilation: how they work and when to use each
Why we network: LAN, WAN, PAN and VPN, and modern digital infrastructure (the internet, cloud, distributed systems, edge computing and mobile networks)
Network devices: network interface cards, switches, routers, wireless access points, modems, gateways and hardware firewalls
Transport and application protocols: TCP and UDP, HTTP and HTTPS, and DHCP
The TCP/IP model: application, transport, internet and network interface layers, and how they work together
Star, mesh and hybrid topologies, and the client–server and peer-to-peer models
Network segmentation: segments, subnetting and VLANs for performance and security
Servers: DNS, DHCP, file, mail, proxy and web servers, and their scalability, reliability and security
IP addressing: IPv4 and IPv6, public and private, static and dynamic addresses, and network address translation (NAT)
Transmission media (fibre, twisted pair and wireless) and packet switching through switches and routers
Static routing and dynamic routing: how each works, and their advantages and disadvantages
Firewalls: filtering traffic with rules, whitelists and blacklists, their strengths and limits, and NAT as extra protection
Encryption: symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, public and private keys, digital certificates and key management
Network vulnerabilities: DDoS, insecure protocols, malware, man-in-the-middle, phishing, SQL injection, XSS, unpatched software, weak authentication and zero-day exploits
Countermeasures: encrypted protocols, MFA, password policies, input validation, CSP, IDS/IPS, DDoS mitigation, email filtering, certificates, VPNs, updates, wireless controls, testing and training
Relational databases: tables, primary, foreign and composite keys and relationships, and their benefits and limitations
Database schemas (conceptual, logical, physical) and choosing data types
Entity relationship diagrams: entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality and modality
Constructing tables with primary, foreign, composite and concatenated keys, and keeping data integrity
Normal forms: 1NF, 2NF and 3NF, atomicity, functional, partial and transitive dependencies
Normalising a real database to 3NF step by step, and when to denormalise for performance
SQL: data definition and data manipulation languages, and SELECT queries with filtering, pattern matching and ordering
Joining two tables, GROUP BY and HAVING, and changing data with INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE (and what that does to indexes)
Aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN) on grouped data, and virtual and materialised views
Transactions and data integrity: ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) and BEGIN TRANSACTION, COMMIT and ROLLBACK
Beyond relational: NoSQL, cloud, spatial and in-memory databases and where each is used
Data warehouses for business intelligence, OLAP, and data-mining techniques
Distributed databases: partitioning, replication, transparency, fault tolerance, concurrency and ACID across sites
Types of machine learning (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, deep and transfer learning) and their real-world uses
Hardware for machine learning: from laptops to GPUs, TPUs, ASICs, FPGAs, edge devices, cloud platforms and HPC centres
Data cleaning: outliers, duplicates, incorrect and irrelevant data, formatting, missing values, normalization and standardization
Feature selection (filter, wrapper and embedded methods) and why dimensionality reduction matters
Linear regression: predicting continuous outcomes, slope and intercept, and r² as a measure of fit
Classification: K-nearest neighbours and decision trees, with recommendation systems and medical diagnosis
Evaluating classifiers: accuracy, precision, recall and F1; hyperparameter tuning; overfitting and underfitting
Unsupervised learning: clustering for customer segmentation and association rules for hidden relationships
Reinforcement learning (agents, states, actions, rewards, policies, exploration v exploitation) and genetic algorithms
Artificial neural networks: the perceptron (inputs, weights, bias, activation, output) and multi-layer perceptrons
Convolutional neural networks for images, and choosing and comparing machine learning models
Ethics of machine learning: bias in training data, fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, consent, security, environmental and societal impact, and online communication
Technology in daily life: reassessing ethical guidelines, and the impact of quantum computing, AR, VR and pervasive AI on society, rights, privacy and equity
Constructing a problem specification: problem statement, constraints, objectives, inputs, outputs and evaluation criteria
The four concepts of computational thinking: decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithmic design
Applying computational thinking to solve problems in software development, data analysis, machine learning, database design and network security
Tracing flowcharts: standard symbols, flow of control, tracking variables and determining output
Variables and data types: Boolean, char, decimal (float/double), integer and string
Global and local variables: scope, lifetime, and tracing programs that use both
Strings and substrings: indexing, length, slicing and searching
Manipulating strings: concatenating, replacing, altering case, trimming and building new strings
Exception handling: points of failure (unexpected input, unavailable resources, logic errors) and try/except/catch/finally
Debugging techniques: trace tables, print statements, breakpoints and step-by-step execution
Robust programs in practice: validating input, handling exceptions and debugging a complete program
Static and dynamic data structures: memory allocation, resizing, speed, memory use and flexibility
One-dimensional arrays and lists: creating, indexing, updating and traversing
Two-dimensional arrays and lists: rows, columns, nested loops and grids
Dynamic lists: adding, removing and traversing elements with Python lists and Java ArrayLists
Stacks: last in, first out (LIFO), with push, pop, peek and isEmpty
Queues: first in, first out (FIFO), with enqueue, dequeue, front and isEmpty
Choosing data structures: arrays, lists, stacks and queues for real problems
Sequence: the order of instructions and its effect on what a program does
Avoiding errors: infinite loops, deadlock and incorrect output
Selection: if, else, elif / else if, and relational operators
Boolean operators AND, OR, NOT in conditions, and controlling program flow with them
Counted loops: for loops, ranges, steps and accumulators
Conditional loops: while and do-while, validation loops, sentinels and choosing the right loop
Functions and modularization: parameters, return values, scope and well-structured reusable code
Efficiency and Big O notation: time and space complexity and scalability
Linear search: construction, tracing and efficiency
Binary search: construction, tracing, efficiency, and choosing between linear and binary search
Bubble sort: construction, tracing, the swapped flag, and time and space complexity
Selection sort: construction, tracing, complexity, and comparing it with bubble sort
Recursion: base case, recursive case, the call stack, advantages and limitations, and quicksort
Constructing and tracing simple, non-branching recursive algorithms in Python and Java
Text files: opening in read, write and append modes, and reading files line by line
Writing, appending and closing text files, and building complete file-processing programs

topics.name: Fundamentals of OOP for a single class

lessons.title: The fundamentals of OOP: classes, objects, inheritance, encapsulation and polymorphism, and when OOP helps
Designing classes with UML class diagrams: attributes, methods, visibility and relationships
Defining classes and instantiating objects: attributes, methods and constructors
Static and non-static (instance) variables and methods: usage, scope and when to use each
Encapsulation and information hiding: private and public, getters and setters, and protecting an object's state

topics.name: Fundamentals of OOP for multiple classes

lessons.title: Inheritance: parent and child classes, "is-a" hierarchies, extends and super
Inheritance and access: private, public, protected and default members in parent and child classes
Extending existing classes: adding members, overriding with super.method(), and the limits of inheritance
Polymorphism and dynamic binding: method overriding, parent references and flexible code
Static polymorphism: method overloading, constructor overloading and compile-time binding
Abstraction in OOP: hiding complexity, modular code and the role of abstract methods
Abstract classes as common interfaces for subclasses, and Java interfaces
Composition and aggregation: building objects from smaller objects, "has-a" relationships and lifetimes
Design patterns and the singleton pattern: one shared instance with global access
The factory pattern: creating objects without naming their exact class
The observer pattern, and choosing design patterns for recurring problems
